title: Accelerator playbook for technical evaluation and contracting
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:
This playbook is designed to accelerate pilot-to-contract conversions for technical buyers (platform engineers, SREs, procurement, and security) evaluating Redwood Inference. It bundles positioning and messaging, a condensed competitive brief, a slide-by-slide pitch outline, pricing guardrails for pilot and enterprise conversion, a short customer case study, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect diligence. Use this during Technical Discovery, Pilot Kickoff, and Contract Negotiation phases.

Target audience:
- Platform engineering leads and SREs evaluating inference performance and reliability
- Security and compliance reviewers assessing data controls and logging
- Procurement and legal teams reviewing commercial terms and SLAs
- Sales engineers and solution architects running pilots

Key outcomes (pilot-run):
1) Validate 95th-percentile token latency targets under representative QPS
2) Demonstrate unit cost improvement vs baseline (target: 20–50% lower TCO)
3) Verify integration controls (VPC, KMS, audit logging) and compliance checks
4) Produce a conversion-ready ROI summary and contract guideline

Value messaging (by stakeholder):
- Platform Engineers: unified runtime across hosted and private deployments, predictable CPU/GPU throughput, kernel-level optimizations, and runtime observability hooks.
- SRE/Operations: SLOs + automatic fallback to compatible model variants, rolling canaries, and token-level tracing for root cause.
- Security: customer-managed keys, audit logs, and VPC private control plane option.
- Procurement/Finance: clear pilot-to-prod conversion pricing bands, reserved capacity discounts, and measurable unit economics for model choices.

Competitive brief (executive summary):
- Redwood differentiators:
  - Production-first runtime: continuous batching, KV-cache-aware paths, optimized kernel selection for mixed sequence lengths.
  - Unified deployment modes: same API & rollout controls for hosted / dedicated / private.
  - Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdown + per-model regression alerts.
- Common competitor gaps to call out:
  - Vendor A: simple API but limited dedicated capacity and weak on private deployment controls.
  - Vendor B: lower sticker price but poor caching and higher per-token inference costs at scale.
  - OSS self-host: full control but long ramp (ops burden) and lack of SLA-backed resilience.

Pitch deck outline (10 slides, 7–12 minute demo narrative):
1) Cover + positioning (1 slide): one-liner and expected outcomes for the pilot.
2) Customer problem (1 slide): operational cost, latency variance, and model lifecycle complexity.
3) Redwood solution overview (1 slide): runtime + orchestration + optimize toolset.
4) Architecture (1 slide): how hosted/dedicated/private map to customer environments.
5) Performance evidence (1 slide): 95p latency, tokens/sec for sample models; include benchmark summary.
6) Security & compliance (1 slide): VPC, KMS, audit logging, SOC2 evidence.
7) Pilot scope & success criteria (1 slide): measurement plan and SLOs.
8) Pricing and conversion paths (1 slide): pilot pricing bands and reserved capacity examples.
9) Case study (1 slide): short result snapshot and metrics.
10) Next steps & contract asks (1 slide): technical contacts, timeline, and commercial checklist.

Pricing guidance (pilot -> conversion):
- Pilot pricing (4-week standard):
  - Small: up to 10M tokens total, dedicated pilot node share, free access to Redwood Console; typical cost: $2,500–$7,500 (fixed) depending on model class.
  - Mid: up to 50M tokens, priority scheduling, pilot optimization consult; typical cost: $10,000–$25,000.
  - Large: bespoke pilot (>50M tokens), reserved pilot capacity with performance SLAs; cost: custom.
- Conversion / enterprise anchoring:
  - Usage pricing: per-token tiers with volume discounts (e.g., 15–40% off list at >1B tokens/month) + embedding unit pricing.
  - Reserved capacity: committed monthly/annual GPU pools with throughput SLAs; typical discount vs hosted: 30–60% depending on commit and hardware.
  - Professional services: migration, private deploy packaging, SLO tuning quoted separately.
- Contract examples to offer in negotiation:
  - 12-month reserved capacity + 3-month pilot credit and 60-day SLA trial.
  - Step-down pricing schedule tied to committed throughput buckets.

Pilot activation checklist (Technical & Commercial):
1) Scope and metrics agreed: representative workload, token mix, latency target, QPS, and success metrics.
2) Data handling decisions: PII masks, retention windows, and whether KV cache persists across requests.
3) Deployment mode selected: hosted vs dedicated pilot node vs customer VPC.
4) Security controls configured: KMS integration, IP allowlists, and audit log export.
5) Instrumentation: Redwood tracing enabled + logs forwarded to customer SIEM.
6) Baseline run: 2-day smoke, 7-day soak, record 95th/99th latency and cost per million tokens.
7) ROI deck prepared and stakeholder review scheduled at pilot end.

Customer case study (example): Nimbus Analytics (fictional)
- Context: mid-market analytics SaaS converted CPU-based reranking to Redwood hosted pipeline.
- Pilot scope: 4-week pilot, 25M tokens, mixed-length prompts, 2M embeddings.
- Outcomes: 35% lower inference unit cost after applying caching & quantization profile; 95p latency reduced from 420ms to 78ms; achieved migration-ready runbook and security checklist.
- Conversion: 12-month reserved capacity with throughput SLAs and a 25% discount on sustained usage.

Security FAQ for prospects (top questions and precise answers):
Q: How do you segregate customer data in Hosted mode?
A: Multi-tenant logical separation, customer-scoped storage for artifacts, optional VPC/private control plane for strict network isolation, and audit logs per tenant.

Q: What encryption options exist for keys and data at rest?
A: Customer keys supported via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and HSM-backed key wrapping available for Private deployments.

Q: Can we run Redwood inside our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane with on-prem installers or VPC peering for private deployments; refer to the "onprem-packaging" guide for platform requirements.

Q: What evidence do you provide for audits?
A: SOC2 Type II reports, config-level audit logs, per-token access traces (subject to retention policy), and optional architecture diagrams and runbooks for third-party audit reviews.

Q: How are secrets and API keys rotated and stored?
A: Secrets are stored encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS in private deployments; hosted keys use our secure secrets service with automatic rotation windows that can be customized during contract.

Q: What is the incident response process for security events?
A: We notify customers within defined SLA windows, provide post-incident reports, and offer joint review calls. On Private deployments we provide playbooks and runbooks for local response.

Objections and suggested rebuttals (short):
- Objection: "We can self-host to save money."
  - Rebuttal: Self-host defers ops cost and maintenance risk; Redwood reduces ramp time, provides SLA-backed performance, and operational observability out of the box.
- Objection: "We don’t want data leaving our VPC."
  - Rebuttal: Offer Private deployment + KMS + audit log export; share architecture diagram and SOC2 artifacts.

Conversion play (recommended cadence):
1) Week 0: Technical discovery and contract skeleton sent (SLA and KMS terms preapproved).
2) Week 1: Pilot kickoff, instrumentation, and smoke runs.
3) Week 2–3: Optimization: batching and quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize team.
4) Week 4: Final soak and ROI deliverable; present to stakeholders.
5) Week 5–6: Term negotiation and reserved capacity proposal.
